PARTIES AND RECITALS
A. Parties
This Agreement is entered into between Northstar Analytics Private Limited, a company incorporated under the
Companies Act, 2013, having its principal office at 21 Meridian Business Park, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560103 (the
“Company”), and Arjun Mehta, residing at 44 Lakeview Residency, Pune, Maharashtra 411045 (the “Executive”). B. Purpose
The Company appoints the Executive as Director, Product Strategy. The Executive agrees to provide executive,
strategic, product, and related services. C. Order of precedence
If a Schedule expressly states that it overrides a numbered clause, the Schedule controls only to the stated extent. Otherwise, the main body controls over a Schedule. LexiGuide AI • Fictional Legal Analysis Test Document Page 3



## APPOINTMENT AND TERM

1. APPOINTMENT AND TERM



## Appointment

1.1. Appointment
The appointment begins on 1 October 2026. The Executive shall perform the duties described in this Agreement and
reasonably related executive responsibilities.



## Initial term

1.2. Initial term
The initial contractual term is 24 months, beginning on the Effective Date and ending at 11:59 p.m. IST on 30
September 2028, unless terminated earlier under Section 8.



## Probation

1.3. Probation
The first 6 months constitute probation. During probation, either party may terminate on 30 calendar days' written
notice. The Company may pay in lieu of unserved notice.



## Place and remote work

1.4. Place and remote work
The primary location is Bengaluru. The Executive may work remotely up to 3 days per week with manager approval. A
change of primary work location requires 15 calendar days' prior written notice where reasonably practicable.



## Duties

1.5. Duties
The Executive shall devote professional working time and attention to Company business, maintain accurate records,
comply with lawful policies, and disclose material conflicts.



## COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

2. COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

All undisputed invoices shall be paid within thirty (30) days of receipt.



## Base salary

2.1. Base salary
Annual base salary is INR 2,800,000, paid in twelve equal monthly installments, subject to applicable deductions. Salary
is ordinarily credited on or before the last working day of each calendar month.



## Annual incentive

2.2. Annual incentive
Target annual incentive is 15% of annual base salary. Payment is discretionary and depends on Company profitability,
individual performance, and Board-approved funding. No target is a guaranteed entitlement.



## Salary review

2.3. Salary review
Compensation is reviewed annually in April. A review does not guarantee an increase.



## Benefits

2.4. Benefits
Subject to plan rules, the Executive may participate in health insurance, provident fund, paid leave, and other benefits
generally made available to comparable executives.



## Expenses

2.5. Expenses
Reasonable business expenses are reimbursable when supported by receipts and submitted within 90 days after the
expense is incurred.

LexiGuide AI • Fictional Legal Analysis Test Document Page 4



## PERFORMANCE, POLICIES AND RECORDS

3. PERFORMANCE, POLICIES AND RECORDS



## Performance objectives

3.1. Performance objectives
Initial objectives are: (a) launch the enterprise analytics product by 31 March 2027; (b) maintain quarterly product
review records; and (c) deliver a written annual product strategy by 15 April each year.



## Compliance

3.2. Compliance
The Executive shall comply with applicable law and lawful written policies concerning information security, workplace
conduct, anti-bribery, expenses, records, and data handling.



## Company systems

3.3. Company systems
Company devices and accounts may be used only for legitimate business purposes. The Company may reasonably
monitor Company systems for security, compliance, incident response, and protection of Company assets, subject to
applicable law.



## Records

3.4. Records
Material product decisions, approvals, customer commitments, and intellectual-property records shall be stored in
designated Company systems within 5 business days after creation or receipt.



## Conflicts

3.5. Conflicts
The Executive shall disclose an actual or reasonably apparent conflict of interest in writing within 5 business days after
becoming aware of it.



## INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

4. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY



## Company work product

4.1. Company work product
To the extent permitted by applicable law, rights in inventions, designs, documentation, software, specifications, product
plans, processes, models, and other work product created in the course of employment and relating to Company
business shall belong to the Company.



## Further assurances

4.2. Further assurances
The Executive shall execute reasonable documents needed to evidence or perfect Company rights. The Company shall
reimburse reasonable out-of-pocket filing or registration costs it specifically requests.



## Pre-existing materials

4.3. Pre-existing materials
The Executive retains ownership of materials listed in Schedule B. Any pre-existing material not listed in Schedule B
that is intentionally incorporated into Company work product shall be disclosed within 7 calendar days after
incorporation.



## Third-party materials

4.4. Third-party materials
The Executive shall not knowingly incorporate third-party material into Company deliverables in a manner that violates
applicable license terms or contractual restrictions.



## Moral rights

4.5. Moral rights
To the extent legally permitted, the Executive consents to reasonable acts or omissions necessary to use, modify, or
commercialize Company work product.

LexiGuide AI • Fictional Legal Analysis Test Document Page 5



## CONFIDENTIALITY

5. CONFIDENTIALITY



## Confidential Information

5.1. Confidential Information
Confidential Information includes non-public business plans, source code, product roadmaps, pricing, customer
information, security information, financial information, research, algorithms, models, and other information reasonably
understood to be confidential.



## Permitted use

5.2. Permitted use
The Executive shall use Confidential Information only to perform duties and shall protect it using at least reasonable
care.



## Exclusions

5.3. Exclusions
Confidential Information excludes information demonstrably: (a) publicly available without breach; (b) lawfully known
before disclosure; (c) independently developed without use of Confidential Information; or (d) lawfully received from a
third party without a confidentiality duty.



## Compelled disclosure

5.4. Compelled disclosure
If legally required to disclose Confidential Information, the Executive shall, where legally permitted, give prompt written
notice and disclose only what is required.



## Duration

5.5. Duration
Confidentiality obligations survive for 3 years after termination. Trade-secret obligations continue while information
qualifies as a trade secret under applicable law.



## DATA PROTECTION AND SECURITY

6. DATA PROTECTION AND SECURITY



## Personal data

6.1. Personal data
The parties shall handle personal data in accordance with applicable data-protection law. The Executive shall access
personal data only when necessary for authorized business purposes.



## Security controls

6.2. Security controls
The Executive shall use multi-factor authentication where provided, keep credentials confidential, promptly install
required security updates, and not knowingly disable endpoint security controls.



## Incident reporting

6.3. Incident reporting
A suspected unauthorized disclosure, loss, compromise, or material security incident involving Company information
shall be reported to the Company's security contact within 24 hours after discovery.



## Return and deletion

6.4. Return and deletion
Upon termination, the Executive shall return Company devices and, subject to applicable retention requirements, delete
Company Confidential Information from personally controlled systems within 7 calendar days.

LexiGuide AI • Fictional Legal Analysis Test Document Page 6



## RESTRICTIVE COVENANTS

7. RESTRICTIVE COVENANTS



## Non-solicitation

7.1. Non-solicitation
For 12 months after termination, the Executive shall not knowingly solicit for employment an employee with whom the
Executive had material business contact during the final 12 months, except through general advertisements not targeted
at such employees.



## Customer solicitation

7.2. Customer solicitation
For 12 months after termination, the Executive shall not knowingly solicit a Company customer with whom the
Executive had material business dealings during the final 12 months for a directly competing service, subject to
applicable law.



## Competitive activities

7.3. Competitive activities
For 12 months after termination, the Executive shall not provide substantially similar product-strategy services to a
direct competitor identified on Schedule C within the territories listed there, to the extent permitted by applicable law.
Enforceability may depend on applicable law and circumstances.



## Reasonableness

7.4. Reasonableness
The parties intend these restrictions to protect legitimate confidential-information and customer relationships and not to
impose a broader restriction than reasonably necessary. If a restriction is not enforceable, the remaining provisions
continue to the maximum extent permitted.



## TERMINATION

8. TERMINATION



## Termination by Executive

8.1. Termination by Executive
After probation, the Executive may terminate employment by giving 90 calendar days' written notice. The Company
may waive all or part of the notice period.



## Termination by Company without cause

8.2. Termination by Company without cause
After probation, the Company may terminate employment without cause by giving 90 calendar days' written notice or,
at the Company's option, base salary in lieu of the unserved portion, subject to applicable law.



## Immediate termination for cause

8.3. Immediate termination for cause
The Company may terminate immediately for material misconduct, fraud, willful material breach, serious confidentiality
or security violation, or other grounds permitted by applicable law, subject to any required process.



## Change-in-control termination

8.4. Change-in-control termination
If a Change in Control occurs and the Executive's role is materially reduced within 120 days thereafter, the Executive
may resign within 90 days after written notice of the reduction. Subject to applicable law, the Company shall pay 3
months of base salary as transition compensation.



## Final payments

8.5. Final payments
Upon termination, the Company shall pay earned salary and other amounts legally due, subject to applicable deductions
and plan rules. Unused leave, if payable, is handled under applicable law and policy.

LexiGuide AI • Fictional Legal Analysis Test Document Page 7

All undisputed invoices shall be paid within thirty (30) days of receipt.



## LIABILITY AND INDEMNIFICATION

9. LIABILITY AND INDEMNIFICATION



## Limitation

9.1. Limitation
Except for liability that cannot lawfully be limited, neither party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, or consequential
damages arising from this Agreement.



## Cap

9.2. Cap
To the extent permitted by law, the Company's aggregate contractual liability to the Executive shall not exceed the
greater of INR 3,600,000 or the base salary actually paid during the 12 months preceding the event.



## Carve-outs

9.3. Carve-outs
The liability cap does not apply to amounts that cannot legally be capped, fraud or willful misconduct, or the Company's
obligation to pay earned compensation.



## Executive indemnity

9.4. Executive indemnity
The Executive shall indemnify the Company for direct losses finally determined to result from the Executive's fraud or
willful misconduct, subject to applicable law.



## DISPUTE RESOLUTION

10. DISPUTE RESOLUTION



## Good-faith discussion

10.1. Good-faith discussion
Before arbitration, the parties shall attempt in good faith to resolve a dispute through a meeting between the Company's
General Counsel and the Executive within 15 business days after written notice of dispute.



## Arbitration

10.2. Arbitration
Any dispute not resolved under Section 10.1 shall be finally resolved by arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation
Act, 1996, as amended.



## Seat and venue

10.3. Seat and venue
The seat of arbitration is Bengaluru, Maharashtra. Hearings may be conducted virtually or at another venue agreed by
the parties.



## Tribunal

10.4. Tribunal
The arbitration shall be conducted by a single arbitrator appointed by mutual agreement. If the parties cannot agree
within 15 days, appointment shall occur in accordance with applicable law.



## Language

10.5. Language
The language of arbitration shall be English.



## Interim relief

10.6. Interim relief
Nothing prevents either party from seeking urgent interim or protective relief from a court of competent jurisdiction
where permitted by law.



## GOVERNING LAW

11. GOVERNING LAW



## Law

11.1. Law
This Agreement is governed by the laws of India, without regard to conflict-of-law principles to the extent such
principles would select another law.



## Court jurisdiction

11.2. Court jurisdiction
Subject to arbitration, courts having jurisdiction over the arbitration seat may be approached for matters permitted by
applicable law.

LexiGuide AI • Fictional Legal Analysis Test Document Page 8



## GENERAL TERMS

12. GENERAL TERMS



## Notices

12.1. Notices
Formal notices must be in writing and delivered by hand, reputable courier, or email to the addresses in Schedule A.
Email notices are effective when the sender receives a non-automated acknowledgment, provided termination notices
are also sent by courier within 2 business days.



## Assignment

12.2. Assignment
The Company may assign this Agreement to an affiliate or successor in a reorganization or transfer of substantially all
relevant business assets. The Executive may not assign this Agreement without written consent.



## Amendment

12.3. Amendment
An amendment must be in writing and signed by both parties, except that the Company may update generally
applicable policies when the update does not materially reduce an express contractual benefit.



## Severability

12.4. Severability
If a provision is held invalid or unenforceable, it shall be modified only to the minimum extent necessary where legally
permitted, and the remaining provisions remain effective.



## Waiver

12.5. Waiver
A failure to enforce a provision is not a waiver of future enforcement.



## Entire agreement

12.6. Entire agreement
This Agreement and its schedules constitute the entire agreement concerning the subject matter and supersede prior
written or oral understandings concerning that subject matter.



## Counterparts and electronic signatures

12.7. Counterparts and electronic signatures
This Agreement may be executed electronically and in counterparts, each deemed an original and together constituting
one instrument.

## LEAVE AND BENEFITS

SCHEDULE E — LEAVE AND BENEFITS
E.1. Annual leave
The Executive receives 24 working days of annual paid leave per completed year, subject to applicable law and policy.
Requests should ordinarily be submitted at least 10 calendar days in advance, except emergencies.
E.2. Sick leave
Sick leave is administered under applicable law and Company policy.
E.3. Statutory benefits
Statutory benefits, including provident fund and other legally required benefits, apply to the extent applicable.
E.4. Insurance
Eligibility for health insurance is subject to insurer terms and Company plan rules.

LexiGuide AI • Fictional Legal Analysis Test Document Page 11



## SPECIAL COMMERCIAL TERMS

SCHEDULE F — SPECIAL COMMERCIAL TERMS
F.1. Retention award
If the Executive remains continuously employed through 30 September 2028, the Company will pay a retention award
of INR 600,000, subject to applicable tax and provided the Executive is not serving a notice of resignation on that date.
F.2. Early departure
If the Executive resigns before 30 September 2028, the retention award is not payable unless the Company expressly
agrees otherwise in writing.
F.3. Bonus timing
Any approved annual incentive for a completed performance year is ordinarily paid within 90 days after the Board
approves the relevant financial results, subject to plan terms.
F.4. Clawback
To the extent permitted by applicable law and plan terms, an incentive payment may be subject to clawback for fraud,
intentional misconduct, or material financial restatement directly attributable to the Executive's misconduct.



## TRANSITION OBLIGATIONS

SCHEDULE G — TRANSITION OBLIGATIONS
G.1. Knowledge transfer
During the final 15 business days of employment, or such other period reasonably requested, the Executive shall
prepare a transition memo covering active initiatives, material risks, key contacts, outstanding approvals, and system
locations.
G.2. Access return
Company devices, badges, credentials, keys, and physical records shall be returned no later than the final working day
unless the Company gives a different written instruction.
G.3. Customer continuity
The Executive shall reasonably assist with introductions and transition of material customer relationships for up to 20
business days after notice of termination, during normal working hours.
G.4. Post-termination contact
The Company may contact the Executive for factual clarification concerning Company records for up to 60 days after
termination, provided requests are reasonable and do not disclose third-party confidential information.

LexiGuide AI • Fictional Legal Analysis Test Document Page 12



## Schedule B: Invoicing & Disbursement Schedule

Payment of all vendor invoices shall be executed within fifteen (15) days of receipt.



## Section 99: Cybersecurity Incident Disclosure

Vendor must notify all cybersecurity incidents and material data breaches to the Company Security Operations Center within 24 hours of discovery.
